items.claim: The single-verse cut at Jer.6.9 is byte-supported: a bare verse-initial divine formula opens the verse, distinct in shape from the causally subordinated occurrence that governs the preceding unit.
items.evidence: The pointed splice re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.6.9, which opens כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהֹוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת with no preceding particle, while the preceding unit's occurrence at oshb:Jer.6.6 is subordinated, כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת - so the restart asserted here is a byte-real difference of shape and not a second printing of the same header. The mouth is Yahweh's: the formula stands in the prophet's own report, outside any quoted human speech, which is the condition for reading it as a seam signal. The armies-title stack recorded as a signal is byte-present (sweep: 50 verses book-wide carry the koh-amar-YHWH-tsevaot skeleton, 2 of them in this chapter, at Jer.6.6 and Jer.6.9), and the bare koh-amar-YHWH object has 5 sites in this chapter (sweep: 152 verses book-wide), so the recorded signals are correctly typed rather than blended. The front-seam petuchah at MT 6:8 is disclosed under its correct type as tier-3 single-witness corroboration and is not made to drive; no parashah mark and no ketiv/qere note falls inside the verse, so the disclosure set is complete. The imperative הָשֵׁב֙ יָדְךָ֔ later in oshb:Jer.6.9 sits inside the oracle body and is not misclaimed as a seam marker.

items.claim: The stated ground that no tier-1 marker stands inside Jer.6.10-Jer.6.15 is byte-false at three points, and the rejected alternative makes modern paragraphing an affirmative reason to keep the material together.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.6.12 closes נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, the book's densest closure formula (sweep: 162 verses carry the neum-YHWH skeleton, 1 of them in this chapter, at Jer.6.12), standing mid-span between the wrath verses and the corruption indictment this unit declines to separate; and oshb:Jer.6.15 closes אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (sweep: 179 verses carry the bare amar-YHWH skeleton, 6 of them in this chapter). oshb:Jer.6.11 further carries the imperative שְׁפֹ֤ךְ, a command that presupposes a speaker other than the one who has just said he is filled with wrath - the very speaker question held open here. So the blanket wording "without a further imperative, vocative, or formula" is contradicted inside the span itself, and the paired phrase "the absence of any tier-1 marker within it" is byte-false: the postpositive closure formula at 6:12 is exactly a tier-1 device, and it is the one signal that would argue a sub-seam at 6:12/6:13, which is the split being rejected. Separately, the rejected alternative makes WEB's paragraph division an affirmative reason to keep the material together ("both argue for keeping this material together"); modern paragraphing is tier-4 metadata and cannot bear that weight in either direction, and here it is doing the work the undisclosed formula at 6:12 should have been weighed against. The opening splice does re-collate at byte tier against oshb:Jer.6.10, the medium_low confidence with an open speaker question is honest calibration, and the closing setumah at MT 6:15 is disclosed under its correct type - the defect is in the grounds, not necessarily in the span.
tier_citations: tier-4 (modern paragraph division - not boundary evidence)

items.claim: The seam is sound but its stated ground overstates: Jer.6.17 does carry a further imperative, embedded in the watchmen's reported call.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.6.17 reads הַקְשִׁ֖יבוּ לְק֣וֹל שׁוֹפָ֑ר, a command both witnesses render as such (“Listen to the sound of the trumpet!”, web:Jer.6.17), so the wording "without a further imperative or koh-amar restart through the watchmen image of Jer.6.17" is byte-false as written. What is actually true is narrower and would have been the stronger statement: the imperative sits inside reported speech and is answered by וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹ֥א נַקְשִֽׁיב in that same verse, oshb:Jer.6.17, reproducing the command-plus-refusal shape of the verse before it, which is what binds 6:17 to 6:16 rather than what would separate them. The restart claimed at the front seam is byte-true and verse-initial, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה at oshb:Jer.6.16 (sweep: 152 verses carry the koh-amar-YHWH skeleton, 5 of them in this chapter, at Jer.6.6, Jer.6.9, Jer.6.16, Jer.6.21 and Jer.6.22), the mouth is Yahweh's and not a quoted human speaker's, and the front-seam setumah at MT 6:15 is disclosed under its correct type with no other parashah mark or ketiv/qere note inside the span. The boundary itself is not disturbed; the negative-existence claim supporting it is.

items.claim: An addressee turn of exactly the class used to cut the front seam falls inside the span at Jer.6.20, which addresses the offerers and not the witnesses summoned at Jer.6.18-Jer.6.19.
items.evidence: Both splices re-collate at byte tier. oshb:Jer.6.18 summons שִׁמְע֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם and, in the same verse, a second and separate addressee under its own imperative, וּדְעִ֥י עֵדָ֖ה, whose terminal yod contrasts with the terminal vav of the plural imperative beside it; oshb:Jer.6.19 summons שִׁמְעִ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ on that same shorter pattern, while the body of 6:19 speaks of הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה in the third person. oshb:Jer.6.20 then turns to second-person-plural possessors carrying the kem suffix, עֹלֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ and וְזִבְחֵיכֶ֖ם (“Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices are not pleasing to me.”, web:Jer.6.20) - the cult of the people just described in the third person, not the nations and the earth called as witnesses. The rejected alternative asserts the opposite, that Jer.6.20 "continues the same address to the summoned witnesses"; the bytes contest that, and the same addressee-shift class is what is used to justify the front seam at 6:17/6:18, so the unit applies its own criterion inconsistently. Compounding this, oshb:Jer.6.18 opens with לָכֵ֖ן (sweep: 55 verses carry the lakhen skeleton, 3 of them in this chapter, at Jer.6.15, Jer.6.18 and Jer.6.21), a consequence particle binding the summons back to the refusal reported at Jer.6.16-Jer.6.17; it is quoted but its backward force is not weighed, and unlike Jer.6.21 there is no formula here to override it, yet the confidence is held at high. The closing setumah at MT 6:20 is disclosed under its correct type and is not made to drive.

items.claim: The single-verse cut at Jer.6.21 is byte-supported at both seams, and its ketiv/qere and parashah disclosures are all correct at the byte level.
items.evidence: The splice re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.6.21, which opens לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה, a verse-initial divine restart (sweep: 152 verses carry the koh-amar-YHWH skeleton, 5 of them in this chapter) spoken in the prophet's report rather than inside quoted human speech. The ketiv/qere claim is byte-checkable and correct: the written and read forms stand at the verse's final verb, where they are placed, and outside the pointed splice, so the slicing discipline holds and the inventory count of one note at this verse matches. The back seam is formula-marked on both sides: oshb:Jer.6.22 opens its own verse-initial restart of the same shape on a different subject. The front-seam setumah at MT 6:20 and the petuchah standing at this unit's own verse are disclosed under their correct and distinct types as tier-3 single-witness corroboration, neither conflated nor made to drive. The verse-initial consequence particle here is immediately overridden by a tier-1 formula, which is what distinguishes this case from the bare consequence particle at Jer.6.18 and makes the high confidence calibrated.

items.claim: The Jer.6.22-Jer.6.23 cut is byte-supported at both seams, with no byte-true device straddling either seam undisclosed.
items.evidence: The splice re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.6.22, a verse-initial כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה restart (sweep: 152 verses carry the koh-amar-YHWH skeleton, 5 of them in this chapter) opening a new subject, הִנֵּ֛ה עַ֥ם בָּ֖א מֵאֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֑וֹן, in the prophet's report and not inside quoted human speech. The back seam is byte-marked from both sides: oshb:Jer.6.23 ends עָלַ֖יִךְ בַּת צִיּֽוֹן, still third-person description of the invader delivered to a singular hearer, while oshb:Jer.6.24 opens שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ אֶת שָׁמְע֖וֹ רָפ֣וּ יָדֵ֑ינוּ, a first-person-plural voice both witnesses carry (“We have heard its report. Our hands become feeble.”, web:Jer.6.24). No parashah mark and no ketiv/qere note falls inside Jer.6.22-Jer.6.23; the front-seam petuchah at MT 6:21 is disclosed under its correct type as tier-3 single-witness, so the span-relevant disclosure set is complete. Neither seam is straddled by an undisclosed formula chain, catchword hook or refrain, and the grounds stated here rest on the Hebrew bytes rather than on a rendering choice.

items.claim: The unifying ground, a communal first-person-plural voice across Jer.6.24-Jer.6.25, is carried by 1 of the span's 2 verses: Jer.6.25 has 0 first-person forms, and its 2 ketiv/qere notes fall precisely on the addressee number the label and the back seam both rest on.
items.evidence: oshb:Jer.6.24 carries 3 first-person-plural forms - שָׁמַ֥עְנוּ, יָדֵ֑ינוּ, הֶחֱזִיקַ֔תְנוּ - and both witnesses agree (“We have heard its report. Our hands become feeble.”, web:Jer.6.24); the splice re-collates at byte tier. oshb:Jer.6.25 carries 0 first-person forms and is instead a negative second-person address, and the verse's own bytes carry both readings of its 2 variant notes inline - the written form against the read form at תצאי תֵּֽצְאוּ֙, and again at תלכי תֵּלֵ֑כוּ - the written pair ending in yod against the read pair ending in vav. The notes therefore vary exactly the person-and-number that the unit label asserts and that the back seam at 6:25/6:26 is argued from. The doubled-note count is disclosed correctly and the tokens are kept out of the splice, but what the notes contest is the one thing the grounds assert. Under the written form Jer.6.25 stands in the same singular address paradigm as בַּת עַמִּ֤י חִגְרִי שָׂק֙ and עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ at oshb:Jer.6.26, and oshb:Jer.6.23 already closes עָלַ֖יִךְ בַּת צִיּֽוֹן in that same address class across the front seam, so the material is not cleanly one communal voice on either side. The medium confidence and the note that the cut is not formula-marked are the right calibration; the statement that the front seam at 6:23/6:24 turns on a real first-person-plural onset is byte-true and stands. The absence of a parashah mark at the front seam and inside the span is stated correctly.

items.claim: The voice contrast this cut rests on is byte-contested on both sides of its own front seam: Jer.6.26 itself closes with 1 first-person-plural suffix, and Jer.6.25 has 0 first-person forms.
items.evidence: The splice re-collates at byte tier against oshb:Jer.6.26, and the vocative-plus-imperative onset בַּת עַמִּ֤י חִגְרִי שָׂק֙ is byte-true and verse-initial; the marker-class comparison also holds at the bytes, against כַּבְּסִ֨י מֵרָעָ֤ה לִבֵּךְ֙ with the vocative יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם at oshb:Jer.4.14 and against הָעִ֣זוּ בְּנֵ֣י בִניָמִ֗ן at oshb:Jer.6.1. But oshb:Jer.6.26 ends עָלֵֽינוּ, a first-person-plural suffix both witnesses carry (“for the destroyer will suddenly come on us”, web:Jer.6.26) - the very communal voice this verse is declared distinct from, straddling the front seam and left undisclosed as continuity while the English is quoted as content. And the material it is being separated from does not carry that voice where the contrast is drawn: oshb:Jer.6.25 has 0 first-person forms, its 2 variant notes stand on the addressee number, and under the written form it is the same singular address as וְהִתְפַּלְּשִׁ֣י and עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ at oshb:Jer.6.26, while oshb:Jer.6.23 already closes עָלַ֖יִךְ בַּת צִיּֽוֹן in that class. So both legs of the contrast are byte-contested and the confidence is held at high. The doubled-note disclosure at MT 6:25 and the statement that no parashah mark stands at that verse or inside Jer.6.26 are both correct.
